subject: Performance decision matrix & MOP confirmation for Solstice pilot
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@solstice.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-29T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Performance decision matrix & MOP confirmation for Solstice pilot

Hi Lena —

Thanks again for the demo and for walking through Solstice's production workload. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the proposed performance acceptance matrix and immediate map-of-work (MOP) items so we can lock the pilot gating criteria and next steps. Attaching the spreadsheet and demo recording for reference.

High-level proposal (please confirm or correct):
- Target SLOs (happy path):
  • p95 latency (end-to-end, 512-token generation): <= 120 ms
  • p99 latency (spike tolerance): <= 350 ms
  • Sustained concurrency target: 200 concurrent requests (steady-state)
  • Burst capacity: 300 concurrent requests (10m windows)
  • Streaming first-byte (initial chunk) latency: <= 150 ms
  • Per-stream token-generation baseline: 30 tokens/sec
- Throughput: sustained 1,000 RPS across batchers (average payloads)
- Observability: need metrics exposed for p50/p95/p99, token counts, queue length, and per-route cost/billing tags
- Fallback plan: automatic degrade to quantized L7 variant under sustained overload; preserve semantic fidelity for core intents

Immediate MAP (owner / due):
- Load test plan and scripts (Priyom) / draft by 2028-10-03
- Canary run checklist + rollback criteria (Marcus) / canary window week of 2028-10-09
- Demo recording and trace samples uploaded to shared Drive (Karthik) / done (see attachments)
- Security/VPC integration checklist (Solstice SRE + Redwood infra) / initial sync to schedule

Questions for you:
1) Do you agree with the SLO targets above as the pilot acceptance criteria, or should we adjust p95/p99 and concurrency?
2) Any absolute constraints (e.g., maximum cost per 1k tokens, or max allowed tail-latency during batch windows) we should bake into the decision matrix?
3) Who on your side will own the canary window coordination and SRE liaison?

Attachments: rwi-solstice-performance-matrix.xlsx (matrix + pass/fail criteria), rdw-demo-recording.mp4

If this looks good I'll kick off the internal load-test plan and schedule the canary checklist review with Marcus & Priyom.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Lena Park <lena.park@solstice.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Solstice SRE <sre@solstice.ai>
Date: 2028-09-29T18:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance decision matrix & MOP confirmation for Solstice pilot

Karthik —

Thanks for the tidy summary and the attachments. Quick clarifications from our side after an internal sync with SRE/Platform: 

Adjusted constraints and asks (internal):
- p95: we'd be comfortable moving the p95 target to <= 150 ms for initial acceptance (we can tighten over time)
- p99: must be <= 400 ms under expected peak (spikes during load test considered)
- Concurrency: target 200 sustained, but we require 20% headroom for sudden bursts (so plan for 240 in canary)
- Streaming: initial-chunk (first-byte) <= 200 ms; per-stream sustained token rate ~25 tokens/sec
- Throughput: our expected steady-state is ~800 RPS with spiky bursts to 2k RPS for short periods (1-5 min) — please ensure your load tests include 2k spike scenarios
- Security: VPC peering + KMS envelope flow needs to be validated in the canary (we'll provide contact for our cloud infra)

Attaching a short set of trace excerpts and a sample traffic profile (streaming-trace-samples.jsonl) to help shape the load tests.

Who on your side will propose the concrete canary schedule? We're aiming for the first window the week of 2028-10-09.

On the decision matrix, one non-negotiable for us: p99 under sustained 2k burst should not exceed 600 ms; if it does, we will require a temporary rate-limiter policy while a fallback is engaged.

Thanks —
Lena
Product & Ops Lead | Solstice AI
lena.park@solstice.ai

Date: 2028-09-30T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance decision matrix & MOP confirmation for Solstice pilot

Team — following Lena's note, I've updated the decision matrix and MOP to reflect Solstice constraints. Quick internal callouts and assignments so we move cleanly into canary planning: 

Updated acceptance criteria (agreed baseline for pilot):
- p95 <= 150 ms (512 tokens)
- p99 <= 400 ms under expected peaks; absolute max 600 ms under 2k burst (Solstice requirement)
- Sustained concurrency: 200; plan for 240 (20% headroom)
- Burst capacity: validate up to 2k RPS for short windows with graceful degradation
- Streaming first-byte <= 200 ms; per-stream generation >= 25 tokens/sec

MOP items (owners & checkpoints):
- Load test implementation: Priyom — run baseline steady-state (800 RPS), 1k steady, and 2k short bursts. Deliver: load-test report + artifacts (trace + Grafana dashboards) by 2028-10-04. Attach artifact stub to HubSpot.
- Canary checklist + rollback plan: Marcus — draft runbook and automated rollback hooks (model fallback + rate-limiter profile) by 2028-10-05. Canary window proposal for 2028-10-10.
- Observability wiring: Karthik — ensure p99 alert rules and cost/token breakdown tags are present in the canary dashboard (link in Drive).
- Security/VPC validation: coordinate with Solstice SRE (Lena) to confirm peering and KMS handshake during canary.

Decision points we still need from Solstice before canary:
1) Formal sign-off on the updated p95/p99 and headroom numbers above (Lena)
2) Confirmation of canary window date and SRE on-call contact
3) Any upper-bound cost constraint we should enforce during the canary (to avoid surprise billing)

I'll start the internal load-test cluster tonight and tag the outputs in the shared Drive folder. Priyom — please post the basic run results to the Drive and ping here when done. Marcus — I'll queue a short sync to walk through rollback hooks tomorrow.

Attachments referenced: rwi-solstice-performance-matrix.xlsx, streaming-trace-samples.jsonl

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Lena Park <lena.park@solstice.ai>

Subject: Re: Performance decision matrix & MOP confirmation for Solstice pilot

Karthik / Marcus / Priyom —

All good from our side. We sign off on the updated acceptance criteria (p95 150ms / p99 400ms / headroom 20%). Solstice SRE will own the canary coordination and I will share the on-call rotation later today.

Canary window: 2028-10-10 (morning PST) looks good — we'll reserve the window and provide the SRE contact.

Cost guardrail: please ensure we have a soft cap at $X/day during the canary and automated pause if exceeded; we can tune after the first run.

Thanks — looking forward to the canary.

Lena
Product & Ops Lead | Solstice AI
